# Lua API

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_lua_doc.lua from the documented code, do not edit -->

What the app offers scripts and what scripts offer the app. How scripts work: [lua_scripts.md](lua_scripts.md).

Types: `{ T }` is a list, `{ [K] = V }` a table with keys of type `K`, `or nil` marks a value that may be nil. An integer is a Lua integer.

## Manifests

A script offers a function named after a manifest, e.g. `scripture.read`. The app calls it with the input as a table and takes the output as a table.

### `lookup.translations`

A script that offers this and `lookup.url` opens references in the browser. `Lookup > Scripts` chooses the
script by its name. Until the user chooses, the app uses the script with the most translations. Respect the terms
of use of the web pages a script reads.

Input:

- `language` (`string`): the language of the user, `english` or `german`

Output:

- `names` (`{ string }`): the translations to choose from in `Lookup > Translations`, may be empty. The app shows them as
  they are, so the bundled scripts offer full names, e.g. `Lutherbibel`, and map them to url abbreviations.
- `defaults` (`{ string } or nil`): the translations used until the user chooses some

### `lookup.url`

For a reference over several chapters the app asks once per chapter and opens each url in its own tab.

Input:

- `translations` (`{ string }`): the chosen translations, in the order chosen
- `book` (`string`): the identifier of the app, e.g. `john`
- `chapter` (`integer`): the chapter
- `verse_begin` (`integer`): the first verse
- `verse_end` (`integer`): the last verse

Output:

- `url` (`string or nil`): the web page that shows the verses, or `nil`. The app opens only a valid `http` or `https` url, so
  encode characters that are not ASCII.

### `scripture.names`

A script that offers this and the three manifests below offers scriptures, and several scripts may do so.
The app lists them with its other scriptures, named after the script, e.g. `LUT (Bibleserver)`, and uses the
fallback versification for them. Respect the copyright of the translations.

Output:

- `names` (`{ string }`): the scriptures the script offers, e.g. `{ "ABC" }`

### `scripture.information`

Information about a scripture.

Input:

- `name` (`string`): one of the names the script offers

Output:

- `abbreviation` (`string or nil`): its abbreviation
- `language` (`string or nil`): its language
- `copyright` (`string or nil`): its copyright, shown below the verses

### `scripture.book`

The names of a book in a scripture.

Input:

- `name` (`string`): one of the names the script offers
- `book` (`string`): the identifier of the app, e.g. `john`

Output:

- `abbreviation` (`string or nil`): its abbreviation
- `short_name` (`string or nil`): its short name, shown in the app. Without one the app shows the identifier.
- `long_name` (`string or nil`): its long name

### `scripture.passage`

A verse. The app asks for every verse it shows and keeps nothing,
so the script may ask `workflow.cache` first.

Input:

- `name` (`string`): one of the names the script offers
- `book` (`string`): the identifier of the app, e.g. `john`
- `chapter` (`integer`): the chapter
- `verse` (`integer`): the verse

Output:

- `text` (`string or nil`): its plain text. The app shows markup of a web page as text.
- `error` (`string or nil`): shown in place of a verse without `text`. Without one the app shows `verse not found`.

### `scripture.read`

A script that offers this reads scripture files, those of the scripture folder and those the user imports.
The app asks each reader until one tells the file is of its format, by a name or an error. The app reads the
archive, the script its entries with `workflow.scripture_store.read_entry`. The bundled readers `USX` and
`USFM` read the USX bundles of the Digital Bible Library and zip archives of USFM files.

Input:

- `file` (`string`): the name of the file, e.g. `bible.zip`
- `entries` (`{ string }`): the names of the files in the archive

Output:

- `name` (`string or nil`): the name of the scripture, `nil` if the file is not of a format the script reads
- `abbreviation` (`string or nil`): its abbreviation
- `language` (`string or nil`): its language
- `copyright` (`string or nil`): its copyright, shown below the verses
- `book_names` (`{ [string] = { [string] = string } } or nil`): the names of the books by the identifier of the app,
  e.g. `john`: `abbreviation`, `short_name` shown in the app, and `long_name`
- `verses` (`{ [string] = { [integer] = { [integer] = string } } } or nil`): the text of every verse the scripture numbers, by book, chapter and verse. The app derives the
  versification from them, a book left out takes the one of the closest default versification. Each verse is a
  sequence of paragraph sections `<p data-id="...">`: `begin` for a verse that opens its paragraph, `continue`
  for one that continues it and `undefined` outside of paragraphs. Inside, `<b>` and `<i>` mark text up, and
  `&`, `<` and `>` are escaped. A verse without text of its own is empty, e.g. 3 and 4 of a verse "2-4".
- `cross_references` (`{ [string] = { [integer] = { [integer] = { string } } } } or nil`): the cross references of the verses by book, chapter and verse
- `error` (`string or nil`): why a file of its format can not be read

## Functions

What the app offers at `workflow`.

### `workflow.cache.get(name, key)`

Reads a text value from a cache. A cache keeps its values after the app closes. Each cache is the SQLite file
`cache/<name>.sqlite` in the local data folder, and other programs may read and change it. A cache that fails is
logged and holds nothing.

- `name` (`string`): the cache, made of letters, digits and `_`. Each script uses its own cache.
- `key` (`string`): the key of the value
- Returns the value, or `nil` if there is none

### `workflow.cache.set(name, key, value)`

Writes a text value to a cache, see `workflow.cache.get`.

- `name` (`string`): the cache
- `key` (`string`): the key of the value
- `value` (`string or nil`): the value, `nil` removes the key

### `workflow.scripture.scripture_count()`

- Returns the number of scriptures, including those of scripts

### `workflow.scripture.book_identifiers()`

- Returns the identifiers of all books, e.g. `john`

### `workflow.scripture.name(scripture_name)`

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its name, or `nil` if there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.abbreviation(scripture_name)`

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its abbreviation, or `nil` if there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.language(scripture_name)`

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its language, or `nil` if there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.copyright(scripture_name)`

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its copyright, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.book_abbreviation(scripture_name, book_id)`

An unknown book raises an error.

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id` (`string`): the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- Returns the abbreviation of the book, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.book_short_name(scripture_name, book_id)`

An unknown book raises an error.

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id` (`string`): the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- Returns the short name of the book, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.book_long_name(scripture_name, book_id)`

An unknown book raises an error.

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id` (`string`): the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- Returns the long name of the book, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

### `workflow.scripture.passage(scripture_name, book_id, chapter, verse)`

A script that asks for a passage of its own scripture calls itself.

- `scripture_name` (`string or nil`): the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id` (`string`): the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- `chapter` (`integer`): the chapter
- `verse` (`integer`): the verse
- Returns the verse with the markup of the app, or `nil` and the reason, e.g. `scripture not found`

### `workflow.scripture_store.read_entry(name)`

Reads an entry of the archive a reader reads, see the
manifest `scripture.read`. It exists only while a reader runs.

- `name` (`string`): the name of the entry, one of the `entries` of the input
- Returns its content, or `nil` and `not found`

### `workflow.web.fetch(url)`

Fetches a web page. The script waits for the page, and other scripts wait too. During
`Web > Pause after a failure` a failed url is not requested again, it returns the same failure.

- `url` (`string`): the address of the page, http or https
- Returns the content of the page, or `nil` and the reason: `invalid_url`, `not_found` (HTTP 404 or 410),
  `timeout` (after 30 s), `init_failed` or `request_failed`

## Settings

Settings of the app at `workflow.setting`, each with the functions at the end, `<setting>` stands for one of them.

### `workflow.setting.scripture.default_name`

The name of the default scripture, `Scripture > Default name`, `nil` for none. Functions called with `nil` as
scripture name use it, so without a default scripture they find no scripture.

### `workflow.setting.scripture.fallback_versification_name`

The versification for scriptures that have none, including those of scripts,
`Scripture > Fallback versification`.

### `workflow.setting.web.retry_pause`

How long a failed url is not requested again, `Web > Pause after a failure`. With 0 s a script may
request a failed url again right away.

### `<setting>.get()`

- Returns the value of the setting

### `<setting>.set(value)`

Changes the setting, like the user does in the settings.

- `value`: the new value
- Returns false if the setting rejected `value` or limited it to its range

### `<setting>.postfix()`

- Returns the text shown after the value, e.g. its unit, or an empty text

## Helpers

What the app offers at `util`.

### `util.log_debug(...)`, `util.log_info(...)`, `util.log_warning(...)`, `util.log_error(...)`

Writes to the app log at that level. Scripts have no console and no print.

- `...`: the values, written like print writes them

### `util.split(s, separator)`

- Returns the parts of `s` between the occurrences of the plain string `separator`, empty parts are kept

### `util.trim(s)`

- Returns `s` without the white space at its start and end

### `util.starts_with(s, prefix)`

- Returns true if `s` starts with `prefix`

### `util.ends_with(s, suffix)`

- Returns true if `s` ends with `suffix`

### `util.keys(t)`

- Returns the keys of `t` as list, in no particular order

### `util.contains(t, value)`

- Returns true if a value of `t` equals `value`

### `util.map(t, f)`

- Returns the list of `f` applied to every element of the list `t`

### `util.filter(t, predicate)`

- Returns the elements of the list `t` for which `predicate` is true, in their order

### `util.copy(value)`

- Returns a deep copy of `value`, tables referenced more than once stay shared in the copy and cycles are kept

### `util.dump(value)`

- Returns readable text of `value`, tables are expanded with sorted keys

### `util.at(path)`

- Returns the value at `path` of sections separated by "." in what scripts see, nil if a section is missing

### `util.parse_xml(text)`

- Returns the element tree of the XML document `text`, or nil and the reason if it is not well-formed. An element
  is a table { name, attributes, children }, its attributes by name, its children elements and texts in their order.
  Comments, processing instructions and the document type are left out, CDATA sections are text.

### `util.xml_text(element, without_layout)`

- Returns the text of the element `element` of util.parse_xml and its descendants, with
  `without_layout` without the texts of white space only, the layout of a document

## Bundled scripts

The nodes of the bundled scripts at `scripts`.

### `scripts.dbl.info(text)`

- Returns the `name`, `abbreviation`, `language` and `copyright` of the metadata file `metadata.xml` `text` of a
  bundle, the local ones first, each nil if the file has none, or nil and the reason if it is no XML

### `scripts.ebible.info(text)`

- Returns the `name`, `abbreviation`, `language` and `copyright` of the
  copyright page `copr.htm` `text` of an archive, each nil if the page has none

### `scripts.paratext.info(text)`

- Returns the `name`, `abbreviation`, `language` and `copyright` of the settings file `Settings.xml` `text` of a
  project, each nil if the file has none, or nil and the reason if it is no XML

### `scripts.scripture_archive.find(entries, file_name)`

- Returns the entry of `entries` named `file_name` in any folder, the one closest to the archive root, nil if none

### `scripts.scripture_archive.read(name)`

- Returns the text of the entry `name` of the archive being read, without a
  byte order mark, or nil and the reason, e.g. for a text that is no UTF-8

### `scripts.scripture_archive.read_scripture(input, format)`

- Returns the scripture of the archive of `input`, the input of `scripture.read`, in the format `format`: a node
  like scripts.usx with the `extensions` of its files, `parse` and `book`. None if the archive holds no file of the
  format, an error if it holds no book of the app. Each file names its book, the first file of a book is read.

### `scripts.usfm.parse(text)`

- Returns the element tree of the USFM document `text` as scripts.usx.parse gives it for USX, or nil
  and the reason if it identifies no book. A usx root holds book, chapter, para, table, sidebar and
  periph elements, paragraphs hold verse, char, ref, note, ms, figure and optbreak elements. Markers
  USFM does not define are character styles. Chapters and verses have no sid and eid, as in USX 2.

### `scripts.usfm.book(tree)`

- Returns the book of the element tree `tree` of scripts.usfm.parse, see scripts.usx.book

### `scripts.usx.parse(text)`

- Returns the element tree of the USX document `text` as util.parse_xml
  gives it, or nil and the reason if it is no USX document

### `scripts.usx.book(tree)`

- Returns the book of the element tree `tree` of scripts.usx.parse or scripts.usfm.parse: its identifier `id` in the
  app, nil for a book the app does not know, its `code`, its `names` (`abbreviation`, `short_name`, `long_name`) from
  the headers before its first chapter, and its `verses` in the markup of `scripture.read` and their
  `cross_references` by chapter and verse. A verse reaches from its marker up to the next one and may span several
  paragraphs. Each verse the book numbers is in it, empty if it has no text of its own, e.g. 3 and 4 of a verse "2-4".

## Lua

The functions of Lua that work differently for scripts.

### `setmetatable(table, metatable)`

Lua's setmetatable, a finalizer fails: Lua runs it without hooks, the shutdown could not stop it.

- Returns `table`

### `load(chunk, name, _, environment)`

Lua's load for text only, damaged bytecode crashes the app. By default the chunk gets globals of its own.

- Returns the loaded chunk, or nil and the error
